THE PARLIAMENTARY DEBATES OFFICIAL REPORT  
IN TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY SESSION OF THE RAJYA SABHA 
Commencing on the 9th November, 2010/18th Kartika, 1932 (Saka) 

RAJYA SABHA 
Tuesday, the 9th November, 2010/18th Kartika 1932 (Saka) 
The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
(The National Anthem, “Jana Gana Mana”, was played.) 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shrimati Jamuna Devi, former Member of this House, Shri 
Arjun Kumar Sengupta, sitting Member of this House and Shri S.S. 
Chandran, former Member of this House. 
Shrimati Jamuna Devi passed away on the 24th September, 2010, at the 
age of 80 years, after prolonged illness. 
Born in November 1929 in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, Shrimati 
Jamuna Devi had her education at Canadian Mission Girls' High School, 
Indore. A political and social worker, Shrimati Jamuna Devi worked for 
the upliftment of tribal village women and children. She was Member, 
Central Adivasi Advisory Board, Government of India, from 1962 to 1967 
and Central Social Welfare Board. 
Shrimati Jamuna Devi started her legislative career in 1952 as a 
Member of the first Assembly of the Madhya Bharat State. She was re-
elected to the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly on five occasions. 
Shrimati Jamuna Devi served as Minister of State (Independent Charge) for 
the Welfare of Tribais, Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, in 1985 
and as Minister of Social Welfare, Women and Child Development, in 1993 
in the Madhya Pradesh Government. She was appointed as Deputy Chief 
Minister of Madhya Pradesh in 1998 and was Leader of the Opposition, 
Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly, from 2003 to 2008 and again, from 
2009 till her sad demise. Shrimati Jamuna Devi also served as a Member of 
the Third Lok Sabha from 1962 to 1967. 
Shrimati Jamuna Devi represented the State of Madhya Pradesh in this 
House from April, 1978 to April, 1980. 
In the passing away of Shrimati Jamuna Devi, the country has lost a 

 2 
noted social worker and a veteran parliamentarian. 

 3 
Shri Arjun Kumar Sengupta passed away on the 26th of September, 2010, 
at the age of 73 years. 
Born in June 1937, at Kolkata, West Bengal, Shri Sengupta had his 
education at Mitra Institution, Bavanipur, Kolkata; Presidency College, 
University of Calcutta; and Massachusetts Institute of Technology, USA. 
An economist and a diplomat by profession, Shri Arjun Kumar Sengupta 
held several distinguished posts and served in many important capacities. 
He was Special Secretary to the Prime Minister of India from 1981 to 
1984; Executive Director and Special Advisory to the Managing Director, 
International Monetary Fund, Washington DC from 1985 to 1990; Ambassador 
of India to the European Union, Brussels, from 1990 to 1993; Member and 
Member Secretary, Planning Commission, Government of India from 1993 to 
1998. 
Shri Sengupta served as an Independent Expert for the Human Rights 
Commission, Geneva on the Right to Development from 1999 to 2004 and 
Human Rights and Extreme Poverty from 2004 to 2006. He taught and 
delivered lectures on Human Rights and Economic Development at Harvard 
University, Essex, University and Oslo University, among others. Shri 
Sengupta held the position of Chairman, Centre for Development and Human 
Rights, New Delhi and Member, High Level Commission of the Legal 
Empowerment of the Poor, UNDP, New York. 
Shri Sengupta chaired the National Commission for Enterprises in the 
Unorganised Sector and will always be remembered for his report on the 
Unorganised Sector, which is the reference document for providing minimum 
social security for all unorganized workers. He also published a book 
'Reforms, Equity and the IMF, 2001'. 
Shri Sengupta represented the State of West Bengal in this House from 
August 2005 till his sad demise. 
Shri Sengupta will be remembered for enriching public life by his 
intellect and ideas. The proceedings of the House bear testimony to his 
deep understanding of the problems of the people. 

 4 
In the passing away of Shri Arjun Kumar Sengupta, the country has 
lost an eminent economist, a noted diplomat and an able parliamentarian. 

 5 
Shri S.S. Chandran passed away on the 9th of October, 2010 at the age 
of 69 years. 
Shri Chandran was born in May 1941 in Sivagangai District of Tamil 
Nadu. A political and a social worker, Shri Chandran was also a noted 
Cine Artiste and had acted as a comedian in more than 700 Tamil films. He 
was the recipient of the 'Kalaimamani' award instituted by the Government 
of Tamil Nadu. Shri Chandran was also Vice- President of the South Indian 
Cine Artistes' Association. 
Shri S.S. Chandran represented the State of Tamil Nadu in this House 
from July, 2001 to July, 2007. 
In the passing away of Shri S.S. Chandran, the country has lost an 
eminent Cine Artiste and an able parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shrimati Jamuna Devi, Shri Arjun 
Kumar Sengupta and Shri S.S. Chandran. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary- General will convey to the members of the 
bereaved families our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy.

MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are aware, large- scale 
destruction, damage to property and tragic loss of lives occurred due to

I am sure the whole House will join me in expressing our heartfelt 
condolences to the Government, Parliament and the people of Indonesia for 
the tragic loss of lives and damage to property caused by the Tsunami in 
the Mentawai Islands off Sumatra and eruption of Mount Merapi in Java.
